name: Recognise major architectural styles
blurb: A dozen styles with diagnostic features turns any walk through an old town into a readable timeline. Windows, arches and roofs do most of the identifying.
gear: An illustrated guide to architectural styles
steps: Learn the diagnostic features rather than dates: round arches for Romanesque, pointed arches and flying buttresses for Gothic, columns and symmetry for Neoclassical.
Learn the domestic styles common where you live — Georgian, Victorian, Arts and Crafts, Art Deco, Modernist, Brutalist.
Learn to read windows: proportion, glazing bars, and sash versus casement date a building quickly.
Learn the modern vocabulary: curtain walls, ribbon windows, exposed concrete, pilotis.
Walk a mixed street and date each building, then check against local records.
Photograph examples of each style and build a personal reference set.
tips: Most old buildings are hybrids, altered over centuries. Look for the original core and the later additions.
Revival styles deliberately imitate older ones. Materials and construction usually give away the real date.
proof: You walk a historic street and correctly identify the style and rough period of most buildings.
